lines: Imagine falling from the sky through a violent storm and waking up alone in a deadly jungle.
On 24 December 1971 a passenger plane is struck by lightning and breaks apart midair.
Seventeen year old Juliane Koepcke falls about 3000 meters while still strapped to her seat row.
She wakes up on the dark forest floor with a broken collarbone and a deep arm cut.
She also suffers from a painful eye injury and a severe concussion after the terrifying plunge.
Her biologist father previously taught her that following flowing water always leads back to people.
She finds a tiny creek and begins walking through the dense and dangerous Peruvian rainforest.
Days pass slowly as she follows the winding water toward a larger and safer river.
Up to 14 other passengers survive the initial crash but tragically die before any rescue arrives.
She spends 11 long days completely alone in the unforgiving jungle facing unimaginable odds.
After 9 days of difficult travel she finally discovers a remote lumberjack camp by the river.
She is found by local workers who provide medical help and bring her back to safety.
Juliane remains the only official survivor of LANSA Flight 508 against all odds and expectations.
Would you have the mental strength to survive 11 days alone in the dangerous rainforest?

lines: If you hear a tsunami siren on a dark beach, do not try to run away in your car.
Japan 2011 surveys show about a third of evacuees got stuck in traffic jams fast.
Mark stands on the sand at night when the sea suddenly pulls back far from the shore.
One. He sees the water vanish and knows a dangerous wave is coming right now.
Mark ignores his car and starts to walk to shelter on foot across the dark beach.
He walks fast past terrified people who panic in the coastal town tonight.
Two. He finds a strong reinforced concrete hotel that stands 10 floors high.
Mark enters the building and moves past the lobby without wasting any precious seconds.
Three. He runs up the stairs because he cannot go far from the shore safely.
He climbs higher and higher until he reaches the top of the safe structure.
He goes above the 4th floor to escape the coming dark water below.
Mark finishes his climb and reaches the roof before the ocean strikes the land.
Dark ocean water rushes violently across the beach and floods the empty streets completely.
The wave smashes into the lower levels of the concrete hotel with massive force.
Mark is safe from the water because he followed every single official safety rule.
It was the perfect plan for surviving the disaster.
There was just one problem.
The first wave is often not the biggest, and the freezing night air is turning into snow.
part1.cliffhanger: The first wave hit, but temperatures are plummeting and snow is starting to fall on the open roof.
